references.text: Fire from the Lord that consumes the sacrifice, a miraculous sign of God's acceptance of the offering
The angel of the Lord touches the sacrifice with his staff, and fire rises from the rock and consumes the meat and the unleavened cakes, just as in Manoah's case
Gideon also offers a young goat and unleavened bread on a rock, parallel to Manoah's offering
The Lord's fire falls and consumes the burnt offering, a sign of God's miraculous intervention
Fire from heaven consumes the sacrifice on the altar, a sign of God's acceptance
The Lord does wonderful things; the expression 'mafli la'asot' (wonderful to do) is linked to God's miraculous acts
The angel of the Lord says that his name is wonderful (peli), explaining the wonder that happened with the sacrifice
